mechanism: Trail word pair = IP word (A4 xx) + CS word (FAR_SEG lo, hi). AL must stay A2h (A4 = MOVSB rebuild trigger), so the lattice in-page offset is fixed by FAR_SEG mod 16: in-page = A2h + 10h*(FAR_SEG mod 16) mod 100h. Engine (Cpu.java): 0F invalid, F6 /1 and F7 /1 invalid, FB = STI valid (1 turn), F1 invalid, F0/F4 unsupported. With FB 0F, an opponent entering at the CS low byte dies after one extra turn (STI then 0F); with F6 0F / F7 0F it dies on the first byte. Entering at A4 or xx behaves the same for all choices (imm16 opcodes in xx turn the trail into a sled either way). So F6/F7 only buy 1 turn at one entry offset, and they force lattice 02h/12h. Keeping 52h needs FAR_SEG = xxBh: only 6Bh is invalid, but 106Bh faults whenever AH = FCh (A and B visit every AH = 0 mod 4 value), and 0F6Bh loses half the IP range. FB 0F is the only lethal 52h choice with full IP range.

threatFindings.evidence: Static (Cpu.java): it saves only one turn (the STI) at one of four entry offsets. Screen a0xw2 (F7): ALL -0.026, strong -0.125. The loss matches the 12h lattice cost seen at 22h/32h/42h.

threatFindings.evidence: Static: only 6Bh is invalid among xBh low bytes; 106Bh faults at AH=FCh, which A (step 44h) and B (step 2Ch) both reach because AH = 0 mod 4; 0F6Bh loses IPs below 9450h.

recommendation: Do not promote. Keep FAR_SEG 0FFBh. F6/F7 only buy one turn of lethality and force lattice 02h/12h (F7 screen -0.026, strong -0.125). The ablation shows that CS-word lethality has no measurable net value (sled word ALL -0.0004; vs 2 copies of V6 leaders +0.024 n.s.). The first-generation SP-to-anchor distance (150h) does matter (N0B -0.037). Close the card.
